source: Cloudflare API read-only inventory; live route, DNS, Worker script and deployment queries

findings.detail: Cloudflare route matching documentation states the most specific matching route wins. The exact thelingolegacy.com/ route is more specific than thelingolegacy.com/* for the apex root request, so the root Worker should win for /. Verify with live HTTP smoke tests for /, /index.html, and nested paths before relying on the behavior.

Live deployment API identifies active version 2d161fa5-598f-4998-ada8-7ac4c72c3461 for thelingolegacyv-5 (100% traffic); registry version-detail evidence resolves this to v137 while latest uploaded version is v270. Root Worker active version is v1 while latest uploaded is v2. Keep active versions protected pending source/build provenance and smoke validation.
No route or DNS records were changed during this inventory

Current read-only Cloudflare DNS inventory (2026-11-09) confirms the apex A record is configured as proxied with origin target 192.0.2.0, within RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1. This is the Cloudflare zone's configured origin target, not a claim about the public DNS answer. The main Worker source uses its ASSETS binding for non-API requests and has no generic origin fetch; the exact-root Worker is a separate route and its active source/version still needs verification. Keep DNS unchanged until the exact-root Worker, route fallback behavior, and a real origin decision are independently verified.

Cloudflare List Worker Deployments contract states first deployment is latest actively serving traffic. Active deployment and 100% version split IDs captured for the four routed Workers in this inventory.
Live Cloudflare DNS list returned 33 records for the zone; no DNS writes performed.

wrangler.jsonc declares 2 routes, while the live zone assigns 18 routes to thelingolegacyv-5. 16 live primary Worker routes are not represented in wrangler.jsonc. A Wrangler deploy or route reconciliation must not be run until ownership and intended preservation of these additional subdomain routes are established.

Primary Worker v270 alias feat-lingo-master-registry-wave0-2026-11-08 and root Worker v2 alias lingo-root-asklingo-preview are uploaded but not active. Root v2 is explicitly annotated Preview only. Keep active v137/v1 serving until candidate source, assets, bindings, route smoke and rollback are independently accepted.

Read-only review of main worker.js at main commit f3916fe6658845d08c3727da1caecdf4b24387ca confirms non-API requests on thelingolegacyv-5 path are served through env.ASSETS.fetch(request); no generic origin fetch fallback is present in that source. The apex exact-root route is assigned to a separate lingo-flagship-root Worker and its source was not verified in this check. The proxied apex A record remains TEST-NET-1 192.0.2.0. Do not change it or assume it is harmless: verify exact-root Worker behavior, route coverage, error/fallback behavior, and a real origin decision before any DNS change.

Read-only account query on 2026-11-09 found 14 Access applications. All Workers has allow-only policies (account members and explicit operator email). Eight legacy/preview per-worker applications still share the reusable bypass-everyone policy; three new non-reusable public apps cover the resilience fallback, public website routes, and public root. Four legacy apps also contain email_domain matchers whose domain field is a full email address. No policy was changed; owners must classify each destination before any access mutation.
